hero_title: Share sensitive text and files without leaving permanent copies behind.
hero_text: Create encrypted, expiring links for confidential messages and downloads. Add an optional passphrase and let single-use access do the cleanup.
security_text: Payloads are encrypted before storage with per-item keys. Links are opaque, expire automatically, and can be claimed only once.

entra_steps_body: Create a backend API app registration, expose an access_as_user delegated scope, create a frontend SPA app registration with this app login page as the redirect URI, grant the frontend permission to the backend API, grant admin consent if required, and configure token group claims if you plan to map Entra groups to app roles. The browser signs in with MSAL using authorization code with PKCE, receives an access token for the backend API audience, and the backend validates it with Entra OpenID/JWKS metadata before issuing an HTTP-only app session. Do not create or store a client secret for Microsoft login.
ad_steps_body: Choose an internal domain controller or LDAP endpoint reachable by the Ephemeral Link container. Use LDAPS whenever possible, set the base DN that contains allowed users, and use a least-privilege bind DN that can search users. Keep the local admin account available as break-glass access. Never log AD passwords, bind credentials, or directory tokens.
graph_steps_body: Use this setup only for server-side notification delivery. The app uses Microsoft Graph client credentials, so no user mailbox password is stored and no interactive sign-in is required.
graph_step_1: In Microsoft Entra admin center, open App registrations → New registration.
graph_step_2: Name the app registration clearly, for example Ephemeral Link Mailer. Use Accounts in this organizational directory only unless you intentionally need multi-tenant mail delivery.
graph_step_3: Do not add a redirect URI for this mailer app. The Graph sendMail integration uses app-only client credentials, not a browser sign-in callback.
graph_step_4: After creating the app, copy the Directory (tenant) ID into the Ephemeral Link Tenant ID field under Microsoft Graph sendMail.
graph_step_5: Copy the Application (client) ID into the Ephemeral Link Client ID field.
graph_step_6: Open Certificates & secrets → Client secrets → New client secret. Choose a short, managed expiry, create the secret, and copy the secret Value immediately. Paste the Value, not the Secret ID, into the Ephemeral Link Client secret field.
graph_step_7: Open API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Application permissions. Add Mail.Send and remove any broader permissions that are not required.
graph_step_8: Click Grant admin consent for the tenant and confirm that Microsoft Graph Mail.Send shows Granted for your organization.
graph_step_9: Choose the sender mailbox that Graph should send as, for example secure-links@example.com. Enter that mailbox address in Sender mailbox. The mailbox must exist in Exchange Online and be allowed for app-only sending.
graph_step_10: For least privilege, create an Exchange Online application access policy that restricts this app registration to only the approved sender mailbox or a dedicated mail-enabled security group.
graph_step_11: In Ephemeral Link, enable Graph sendMail, save the Tenant ID, Client ID, Client secret, and Sender mailbox, then create a test upload request or notification to verify delivery.
graph_step_12: Store and rotate the client secret securely. Do not paste Graph secrets into logs, tickets, screenshots, browser local storage, or source control.

entra_step_1: Open Microsoft Entra admin center, go to App registrations, and create a backend API app registration for Ephemeral Link.
entra_step_2: Copy the backend API Application (client) ID. This value goes in Backend API Audience.
entra_step_3: In the backend API app, open Expose an API. Set the Application ID URI to api://<backend-api-client-id>, then add a delegated scope named access_as_user.
entra_step_4: Open Token configuration on the backend API app and add a groups claim to access tokens if you plan to map Entra groups to app roles. Prefer group object IDs.
entra_step_5: Create a second app registration for the browser client. In Authentication, add a Single-page application platform and add the exact redirect URI for the login page: <your-app-url>/login, for example https://links.example.com/login.
entra_step_6: Copy the browser app Application (client) ID. This value goes in Frontend Client ID.
entra_step_7: In the browser app API permissions, add a permission to your backend API app and select the delegated access_as_user scope. Grant admin consent if your tenant requires it.
entra_step_8: In Ephemeral Link, fill in Tenant ID, Frontend Client ID, Backend API Audience, and optional Authority URL. Enable Microsoft login only after the login-page SPA redirect URI, API permission, admin consent, and token claims are verified.
entra_step_9: The flow matches M365 Toolbox: the browser signs in with MSAL using authorization code with PKCE, receives an access token for the backend API audience, and the backend validates it with Entra OpenID/JWKS metadata before issuing an HTTP-only app session. Do not create or store a client secret for Microsoft login.
entra_group_mappings_desc: Map Entra security groups to Ephemeral Link roles. Use group object IDs whenever possible. If any mapping is configured, Microsoft users must match one mapped group to sign in.

legal_not_legal_advice: This notice is provided as a practical template and is not legal advice. The operator of each instance should review it with their own legal, security, and compliance teams before production use.
privacy_self_hosted_text: Ephemeral Link is software that may be installed and operated by a company, another organization, or the project author on behalf of a specific deployment. Data is processed by the operator of that instance and by the infrastructure and providers chosen for that instance. The project author, acting only as software author, does not automatically control or access every deployment.
privacy_operator_title: Who is responsible for this instance
privacy_operator_text: The organization or person that deploys, hosts, administers, or offers this specific instance is the operator for that instance. If the project author runs this instance, the author is the operator for this instance. Otherwise, the deploying organization is the operator. The operator is responsible for deciding what data may be shared, defining a legal basis, informing users, managing access, configuring retention, handling data subject requests, and complying with applicable privacy laws such as GDPR.
privacy_data_text: Depending on configuration and user behavior, an instance may process user accounts, names, email addresses, IP addresses, session cookies, CSRF cookies, audit metadata, link metadata, upload-request metadata, uploaded filenames, encrypted secret contents, encrypted files, and email recipient information. Secret payloads are designed to be encrypted and single-use, but the instance operator controls deployment, access, retention, and backups.
privacy_email_text: If email delivery, Microsoft Graph, SMTP relays, hosting, monitoring, or backups are used, those services may process personal data. The instance operator is responsible for choosing providers, configuring them securely, and entering into any required data processing agreements.
privacy_contact_text: For privacy questions, deletion requests, access requests, or incident reports, contact the operator of this specific Ephemeral Link instance. If this instance is operated by the project author, use the contact method provided by that deployment. If it is operated by your company, contact your company administrator or privacy team.
terms_self_hosted_text: Each instance is controlled by its operator. Some instances may be operated by a company or other organization; others may be operated by the project author for a particular customer, team, or environment. The project author is responsible as operator only for instances the author actually hosts or administers, not for independent deployments run by others.
terms_operator_text: The operator is responsible for secure configuration, HTTPS, backups, retention, user management, admin access, email settings, monitoring, incident response, acceptable-use rules, legal notices, support, and compliance with applicable laws and internal policies. Users must follow the operator’s rules and must not share unlawful, harmful, or unauthorized content.
terms_as_is_text: Ephemeral Link is provided under its license without warranties. Security-sensitive deployments require operator review, correct configuration, secure infrastructure, and ongoing maintenance. No software can guarantee that secrets will never be disclosed, lost, misdelivered, accessed by unauthorized parties, or retained by external systems.
terms_liability_text: To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law and the project license, the software authors and contributors are not responsible for losses, damages, data exposure, operational failures, compliance failures, user misuse, misconfiguration, hosting issues, email delivery issues, backup retention, unauthorized access, or incidents arising from deployments they do not operate or control. If the author operates a specific instance, responsibility for that instance is governed by the terms, notices, and agreements applicable to that deployment. Some jurisdictions do not allow certain liability exclusions, so local law may apply.
terms_security_text: Operators should use HTTPS, strong secrets, protected Redis and storage volumes, secure cookies, appropriate TTLs, restricted admin access, separate passphrase sharing, logging controls, backup retention limits, and regular updates. Users should verify recipients and avoid sending passphrases through the same channel as generated links.
privacy_short_text: Ephemeral Link can be self-hosted by companies or operated by the author for a specific organization or customer. The privacy responsibilities belong to whoever operates the specific instance. The operator is responsible for privacy notices, legal basis, retention, access control, providers, and user requests.
privacy_no_intent_title: Information the software does not intentionally collect
privacy_no_intent_text: The software is not designed to intentionally collect sensitive categories of personal data for profiling, advertising, tracking across sites, or resale. Users may still choose to place sensitive personal or business information into secrets or files. The instance operator is responsible for deciding whether such use is allowed and lawful.
privacy_cookies_text: An instance may use essential cookies for language selection, CSRF protection, authentication sessions, and Microsoft sign-in flow state. Server, reverse proxy, container, identity provider, and email provider logs may also contain IP addresses, timestamps, user identifiers, and operational metadata depending on operator configuration.
privacy_retention_text: Secrets and files are intended to expire or be consumed according to configured TTLs. Audit logs, accounts, Redis data, storage volumes, email records, and backups may follow separate retention periods chosen by the instance operator. Operators should document retention, backup deletion, and procedures for access, correction, and deletion requests.
privacy_security_text: The software includes encryption, passphrase support, CSRF protection, rate limiting, secure headers, audit logging, and storage isolation features. These controls still depend on correct deployment. No software or hosting environment can guarantee absolute confidentiality, availability, deliverability, or deletion from external systems.
privacy_disclosure_text: Legal requests, security incidents, and user complaints must be handled by the operator of the specific instance. The project author can only respond for instances the author actually operates or controls. For deployments run by another organization, that organization is responsible for notices, disclosures, investigations, and deletion decisions.
privacy_rights_text: Users should contact the operator of their specific instance to access, correct, export, restrict, or delete personal data where applicable. The project author can fulfill these requests only for instances the author operates or controls; for other self-hosted deployments, the author does not possess the instance data.
terms_summary_text: Ephemeral Link is software for sharing temporary secrets and files. An instance may be operated by a company, another organization, or the project author for a specific deployment. The operator of that instance controls the service and is responsible for lawful use, user access, security configuration, retention, backups, email delivery, and support. The software itself is provided as-is under its license.
terms_definitions_text: “Software” means Ephemeral Link source code, documentation, and distributed artifacts. “Instance” means a deployment of the software. “Operator” means the person or organization administering, hosting, or offering that specific instance; this may be the project author for author-operated deployments. “User content” means secrets, files, filenames, messages, metadata, and other information submitted through an instance.
terms_account_text: Operators and users are responsible for protecting their accounts, passwords, sessions, passphrases, API credentials, identity-provider access, and administrator privileges. Shared or weak admin credentials can expose secrets and metadata. Account resets, access reviews, and recovery processes are handled by the operator of the specific instance.
terms_acceptable_use_text: An instance should not be used to share unlawful material, malware, exploit payloads, harassment, discriminatory or abusive content, fraudulent content, content that violates third-party rights, or data that the user is not authorized to disclose. Operators should define and enforce their own acceptable-use policy.
terms_content_text: Users are responsible for the content they create, upload, email, or share through an instance. Uploading content to an instance gives that instance only the technical permission needed to store, encrypt, transmit, display, download, audit metadata, and delete the content according to the configured workflow.
terms_no_recovery_text: Single-use and expiring links are designed so that secrets and files may become unavailable after viewing, download, expiry, admin burn, cleanup, key loss, storage failure, or operator action. Users should not rely on the software as durable storage or backup.
terms_indemnity_text: Operators and users are responsible for disputes, claims, investigations, or regulatory issues caused by their deployment, configuration, content, users, providers, or use of the software. Where permitted by law, they should not involve authors or contributors in disputes arising from an instance those authors or contributors do not operate or control.
terms_ip_text: The software is provided under the project license. The Ephemeral Link name, documentation, visual assets, and project materials may have separate copyright or trademark interests. Operators should preserve required license notices and should not imply that the authors operate, endorse, or support a specific deployment unless that is true or agreed in writing.
terms_changes_text: These template terms may be updated with the software. Each operator should adapt them to their organization, jurisdiction, and deployment, publish the version that applies to their instance, and notify users when their local terms materially change.
